target_customer: Women in Los Angeles seeking ObGyn care, paying by membership or per visit (250 dollar annual subscription, 300 dollar visit without insurance)
problem: Traditional ObGyn practices misuse physician time, so patients wait; Almond rebuilt back office tech and used a wider mix of care roles for faster in-person and telehealth care.
business_model: Membership plus fee for service clinic with telehealth, later insurance based care

founders.name: Tara Raffi
founders.background_notes: YC page: consultant serving large US hospital systems, built McKinsey's internal tech incubator, early operations and marketing at Factual.

founders.name: Carly Allen
founders.background_notes: YC page: Head of Production for global campaigns for Coca-Cola, Nike and Marriott.

exit.reason: Company closure letter cites the financial realities of healthcare and insurance systems making it increasingly challenging to practice in line with its values (as relayed by a directory page)

competitors.name: Tia
competitors.what: Women's healthcare provider mixing virtual and in-person primary and gynecological care; TechCrunch named it as a competitor

competitors.name: Maven Clinic
competitors.what: Virtual clinic for women's and family health
competitors.traction_then: Valued above 1B dollars after its August 2021 round

technical_complexity.rationale: Clinic operations, scheduling and telehealth are standard software; the difficulty is physical clinic operations, staffing and insurance billing.

defensibility.rationale: Clinic care is a service business with local presence but little protection from copying; Tia and others already offered similar care.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded women's health providers already operated. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Almond; it closed its clinic in March 2026.

market_need_then: Patients faced slow ObGyn access and the company cited physician time misuse; women's health funding was active in 2021 with Maven and Tia raising large rounds.

branding.domain_note: Uses almondobgyn.com (descriptive suffix) per the YC page.

identity.logo: Wordmark that looks more like a wellness label than a doctor's office, described as intentional by The Quality Edit
identity.voice_and_tone: Cheeky tagline 'Elevated care for down there'

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Forbes and Femtech Insider; co-founder is a Chief Brand Officer from CAA marketing, and the trademark ALMOND OBGYN was filed in April 2023.

brand_strength.rationale: A brand led co-founder, a distinctive wellness style and cheeky tagline earned press and review coverage, but there is no evidence of community or growth driven by the brand.

outcome_analysis: Almond launched a Melrose Avenue clinic in 2022, raised a 7 million dollar seed led by True Ventures in November 2022 and invested heavily in brand with a CAA marketing co-founder. A directory page relaying the company's closure letter says it closed in March 2026, citing the financial realities of healthcare and insurance; the unit_economics tag follows that statement, while brand_pull is only a weak inference from press coverage.
notes: Seed: TechCrunch and Femtech Insider say 7M led by True Ventures; the directory page reports an SEC Form D filed 2022-11-23 for 7,198,993 dollars from 42 investors and that Forbes names Offline Ventures (not opened, so not listed as investor). Pre-seed 500K Sept 2022 comes from an aggregator and a single database claim. Closure rests on one directory page relaying the company's own letter (appointments ended 2026-03-20); no independent news found. The YC description says Inactive. Company site returned 404. Education of founders not found. Maven source date is 2021 from an Inc article about 2020 and 2021 funding, with the 110M Series D from a search summary.
